n93127.head: σαλαμάνδρειος
n93127.html:
σαλαμάνδρειος, ον,

of or like a salamander, σ. δάκος Nic. Th. 818.

n93128.head: σαλάμβη
n93128.html:
σαλάμβη, ἡ,

vent-hole, chimney, S. Fr. 1093, Lyc. 98:—σαλάβη Hsch., Phot., but in Lyc. l.c. the metre requires σαλάμβη.

n93130.head: Σαλαμιναφέτης
n93130.html:
Σαλαμιναφέτης, ου, ὁ,

betrayer of Salamis, Sol. 2.4.

n93131.head: Σαλαμίνιος
n93131.html:
Σαλαμίνιος, α, ον, also ος, ον,

Salaminian, of or from Salamis, Hdt. 5.104, etc.: also Σᾰλᾰμῑν-ιακός, ή, όν, Str. 8.2.2; and fem. Σᾰλᾰμῑν-ιάς, άδος, A. Pers. 965 (lyr.).

II Σαλαμινία (sc. ναῦς or τριήρης), ἡ, Ar. Av. 144, Th. 3.33; v. πάραλος III.

n93132.head: Σαλαμίς
n93132.html:
Σαλαμίς (also in Gramm. Σᾰλᾰμίν, Hsch., Eust.ad D.P. 498), gen. ῖνος, ἡ,

Salamis, an island and town of the same name, between Athens and Megara, Il. 2.557, etc.

II a town of Cyprus founded by Teucer of Salamis, h.Hom. 10.4, Hdt. 4.162, etc.; Σαλαμίνη, Suid. s.v. Ἐπιφάνιος.

n93134.head: σάλαξ
n93134.html:
σάλαξ [σᾰ], ακος, ὁ, (σαλάσσω)

minerʼs sieve or riddle, Thphr. or Arist. (Fr. 261) ap. Poll. 10.149; σάλαγξ, Hsch.

n93135.head: σαλάριον
n93135.html:
σαλάριον, τό,

Lat. salarium, salary, POxy. 473.45 (ii A.D.) , etc.: Adj. σαλάριος, μέτρον PMasp. 100.20 (vi A.D.).

n93137.head: σαλάσσω
n93137.html:
σαλάσσω,

= σαλεύω, τινα Nic. Al. 457.

II overload, cram full, σεσαλαγμένος οἴνῳ AP 6.56 (Maced.), cf. 11.57 (Agath.), APl. 16.306 (Leon.); cf. σαλεύω.

n93138.head: σαλέη
n93138.html:
σαλέη,

v. σάλη. σάλεσσι, v. θάλεα.

n93139.head: σάλευμα
n93139.html:
σάλευμα [ᾰ], ατος, τό,

oscillation, in pl., Artem. 1.79 (in marg.); σ. πολεμικὸν ἵππου D.Chr. 63.4.

n93140.head: σαλευομένως
n93140.html:
σαλευομένως, Adv.

shakily, opp. βεβαίως, Phld. Rh. 1.260 S.

n93141.head: σάλευσις
n93141.html:
σάλευσις, εως, ἡ,

oscillation, Arist. Mech. 857a8.

n93142.head: σαλευτός
n93142.html:
σαλευτός, ή, όν,

tottering, unsteady, AP 5.174 (Mel.).

n93143.head: σαλεύω
n93143.html:
σαλεύω, fut. σαλεύσω LXX Wi. 4.19: aor. ἐσάλευσα Isoc. 8.95, AP 11.83:— Pass., fut. σαλευθήσομαι LXX Si. 16.18, Ev.Luc. 21.26: aor. ἐσαλεύθην LXX 1 Ma. 9.13, Act.Ap. 4.31, 2 Ep.Thess. 2.2, v.l. in Isoc. l.c.: pf. σεσάλευμαι (v. infr.): (σάλος):—

cause to rock, make to vibrate or oscillate, c. acc., [τὰς ἀγκύρας] οὐδεὶς χειμὼν σαλεύει Pythag. ap. Stob. 3.1.29; σ. τρικυμίᾳ πέδον, of the sea, Lyc. 475; of an earthquake, AP 11.83 (Lucill.), cf. 259 (Id.): metaph., δόξαν σ. Plu. Col. 2.1123f, cf. S.E. M. 8.56, 337, etc.; σ. τινὰ ἐκ θεμελίων LXX Wi. 4.19; ἐπιστολαὶ δυνάμεναι λίθον σαλεῦσαι heartrending, POxy. 528.12 (ii A.D.); σ. τοὺς ὄχλους stir them up, Act. Ap. 17.13, cf. LXX Si. 28.14:—Pass., to be shaken to and fro, waver, totter, reel, χθὼν σεσάλευται A. Pr. 1081; κύκλος σαλευόμενος Pl. Ti. 79e, cf. Arist. Mech. 857a7, Thphr. Lass. 11; of teeth or nails, to be loosened, Gal. 12.871, Dsc. 5.3; of persons, ἐκ Βρομίου γυῖα σαλευόμενον AP 11.26 (Marc.Arg.), cf. 12.31 (Phan.); ὑφʼ ἡδονῆς σαλευομένη κορώνη Sch. Arat. 1009 (wrongly attributed to Archil., Fr. 102); later simply, stir, move, κατεσχέθην νόσῳ . . ὡς μὴ δύνασθαι μηδὲ σαλεύεσθαι PSI 4.299.4 (iii A.D.).

2 shake in measuring, so as to give good measure, μέτρον σεσαλευμένον Ev.Luc. 6.38; cf. σαλάσσω II.

II intr., move up and down, roll, toss, esp. of ships in a stormy sea or persons in them, σ. ἐν πλοίοις X. Oec. 8.17, cf. Hld. 10.4, etc.: generally, put out to sea, App. Mith. 77: metaph., toss like a ship at sea, to be tempest-tossed, be in sore distress, πόλις γὰρ . . ἄγαν ἤδη σαλεύει S. OT 23; πρόδοτος δὲ . . σ. Ἠλέκτρα Id. El. 1074 (lyr.); ὅταν . . σαλεύῃ πόλις E. Rh. 249 (lyr.), cf. OGI 515.47 (Mylasa, iii A.D.); ἐν νόσοις ἢ γήρᾳ σ. Pl. Lg. 923b, cf. Arist. Pr. 883a34; ἐν κινδύνῳ σ. D.H. 10.11; σ. ὑπὲρ ἑαυτοῦ Ael. Fr. 48; to be unstable, Poll. 6.121; flicker, of the eye-balls in nystagmus, Gal. 18(2).68; oscillate, of the λόγος ἐνδιάθετος, ἐν τούτοις S.E. P. 1.65.

2 of ships also, ἐπʼ ἀγκυρῶν ride at anchor, Polyaen. 2.2.7: metaph., ὡς ἐπʼ ἀγκύρας τῆς φύσεως σ. Plu. Am. prol. 2.493d; σ. ἐπὶ τῶν ἐλπίδων Hld. 1.26; also ὁρῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ τούτῳ μόνῳ (sc. τῷ υἱῷ) σαλεύοντας Plu. Demetr. 38; γραῦν ἐπὶ ἑνὶ γομφίῳ σ. Alciphr. 3.28, cf. POxy. 472.50 (ii A.D.); ἐπὶ τοιούτοις παραγγέλμασιν S.E. M. 2.12 (hence later in a causal sense, σ. ἐπί τινι τὰς ἐλπίδας anchor them upon . ., Hld. 2.33).

3 metaph., roll like a ship, roll in oneʼs walk, of persons with the hip-joints far apart, Hp. Art. 56.

n93144.head: σάλη
n93144.html:
σάλη, Dor. σάλα, ἡ,

= φροντίς (cf. σάλος II.2), Hsch., Phot., EM 151.47: also σαλέη, Hsch.

II both σαλέη and σάλη = βλάβη, Id. σαλητόν, v. σάρητον.

n93145.head: σαλία
n93145.html: σαλία πλέγμα καλάθῳ ὅμοιον, ὃ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς φοροῦσιν αἱ Λάκαιναι, οἱ δὲ θολία, Hsch.

n93147.head: σαλία
n93147.html:
σαλία, Dor. for τηλία,

sifter, dub. in Supp.Epigr. 1.414 (Crete, v/iv B.C.).

n93149.head: σαλιούγκα
n93149.html:
σαλιούγκα, ἡ, =

saliunca, Κελτικὴ νάρδος, Dsc. 1.8, Plin. HN 21.42.

n93150.head: σαλκᾶ
n93150.html:
σαλκᾶ (gen. sg.),

a fragrant oil, Aët. 1.135, 12.49.

n93151.head: σάλκαθον
n93151.html: σάλκαθον (?), τό, dub. sens. in Stud.Pal. 20.96.7 (iv A.D.).

n93152.head: σαλκόν
n93152.html: σαλκόν, τό, dub. sens. in PLond. 5.1904.5 (v/vi A.D.).

n93154.head: Σαλμακίς
n93154.html: Σαλμακίς, ίδος, ἡ, a district in Halicarnassus, SIG 46.24 (v B.C.); also a fountain there, said to cause sexual weakness and associated with Hermaphroditus, Str. 14.2.16, Vitr. 2.8.11, Ov. Met. 4.286: hence σαλμᾰκίδες, αἱ, a name for ἑταῖραι (so Suid.) or effeminate men, AP 7.222 (Phld.).

n93155.head: σαλόομαι
n93155.html:
σαλόομαι, Pass.,

go delicately, EM 270.40.

n93156.head: σάλος
n93156.html:
σάλος [ᾰ], ὁ,

tossing motion, of an earthquake, χθονὸς νῶτα σεισθῆναι σάλῳ E. IT 46; esp. rolling swell of the sea, πόντου σ., πόντιος σ., Id. Hec. 28, IT 1443: pl., πόντιοι σ. Id. Or. 994 (lyr.).

2 open roadstead, roads, opp. a harbour, ἐν σάλῳ στῆναι, = σαλεύειν II.2; ἀλίμενον μὲν σάλους δὲ ἔχον Plb. 1.53.10; οὔτε λιμὴν οὔτε σ. ἐπʼ ἀγκύρας D.S. 3.44, cf. Agatharch. 92, Peripl.M.Rubr. 7 (pl.), 55.

II of ships or persons in them, tossing on the sea, ἐκ πολλοῦ σ. εὕδοντʼ ἐπʼ ἀκτῆς S. Ph. 271; σάλον εἶχεν ἡ θάλασσα Plu. Luc. 10; καρηβαρεῖν ὑπὸ σ. Luc. Herm. 28; ἐν τοσούτῳ σ. ναυτιάσαντα Id. Tox. 19: metaph. of the ship of the state, τὰ μὲν δὴ πόλεος θεοὶ πολλῷ σ. σείσαντες ὤρθωσαν πάλιν S. Ant. 163; πόλις . . σαλεύει κἀνακουφίσαι κάρα βυθῶν ἔτʼ οὐχ οἵα τε φοινίου σάλου Id. OT 24; ἐν σάλῳ πόλις γενομένη Lys. 6.49; ἔσχε . . ὁ ἀγὼν ὑποτροπὴν καὶ σ. began to waver, Plu. Alex. 32, cf. Aem. 18; cf. σαλεύω II.1.

2 distemper, restlessness, perplexity, LXX Si. 40.5, Gal. 9.816; τῆς ψυχῆς Max.Tyr. 1.1.

corr.why: In S. OT 24 the adjective qualifies genitive σάλου ('of the bloody swell'); current φοινίον (acc./neut.) cannot agree with σάλου and is a ν/υ misreading. B's φοινίου is the grammatical reading.

n93157.head: σαλός
n93157.html:
σαλός, ή, όν,

silly, imbecile, Hsch. s.v. ὑσθλός, Sch. Ar. Nu. 397.

n93158.head: σαλούσιον
n93158.html: σαλούσιον, τό, ὀρτύγων σ. dub. sens. in PSI 4.428.55 (iii B.C.), cf. PCair.Zen. 12.44, 672.4 (pl.).

n93159.head: σάλπη
n93159.html:
σάλπη, ἡ,

a sea-fish, the saupe, Box salpa, Epich. 63, Arist. HA 543a8, al. (ὃν καὶ βοῦν [leg. βῶκα] καλοῦσιν, Hsch.): also σάλπης, ὁ, Archipp. 19; σάλπος is v.l. in Arist. HA 534a16; σάρπη, ib. 534a9, 621b7; σάλπιγξ, ib. 543a8.

n93160.head: σαλπίγγιον
n93160.html:
σαλπίγγιον, τό,

Dim. of σάλπιγξ, tube, Gal. 2.707; prop. a little trumpet, Hsch. s.v. ἰσκάνδιον.

2 name of a plant, = ἵππουρις, Gp. 2.6.27.

n93162.head: σαλπιγγολογχυπηνάδαι
n93162.html:
σαλπιγγολογχυπηνάδαι, οἱ,

lancer-whiskered trumpeters, Ar. Ra. 966.

n93163.head: σαλπιγγωτός
n93163.html:
σαλπιγγωτός, ή, όν,

trumpet-shaped, λυχνία CIG 3071.8 (Teos), Hsch. s.v. ἰσκανδωτόν.

n93164.head: σαλπιγκτής
n93164.html:
σαλπιγκτής, οῦ, ὁ,

trumpeter, Th. 6.69, X. An. 4.3.29, Ascl. Tact. 2.9, 6.3, etc.; this spelling has the best MS. authority and occurs in Phld. Rh. 2.299 S., but has not been found in Att. Inscrr.; σαλπικτής, SIG 153.68 (Delos, iv B.C.), IG 3.1288, POxy. 519.16 (ii A.D.), etc.; Boeot. σαλπικτάς IG 7.1773 (Thespiae, ii A.D.), σαλπιγκτάς ib. 3195 (Orchom., i B.C.); later σαλπιστής, ib. 9(2).525.4 (Thessaly, ii B.C.), 3.1285 (Attica, i A.D.), 7.3196 (Orchom. Boeot.), Sammelb. 4591.3, etc.; also in Plb. 1.45.13, D.H. 4.17, Apoc. 18.22, etc.

2 = ὄρνις ὁμοίως σάλπιγγι φθεγγόμενος, Phot.; = ὀρχίλος, Hsch.

n93165.head: σάλπιγξ
n93165.html:
σάλπιγξ, ιγγος, ἡ,

war-trumpet, ὅτε τʼ ἴαχε σάλπιγξ Il. 18.219; σ. ἡ ἱερά Artem. 1.56, cf. Lyd. Mens. 4.73:—on various σάλπιγγες, v. Poll. 4.85 sq., Sch.Il. l.c.:—σ. Τυρσηνική A. Eu. 568, E. Ph. 1378, Heracl. 831; ὑπαὶ σάλπιγγος by sound of trumpet, S. El. 711, cf. Ar. Ach. 1001; also ἀπὸ σ. X. Eq.Mag. 3.12, Plb. 4.13.1.

2 metaph., Πιερικὰ σ., of Pindar, AP 7.34 (Antip. Sid.); οὐρανίη σ. thunder, Tryph. 327, Nonn. D. 2.558.

II = σάλπισμα, ap. Arist. Rh. 1408a9.

III σ. θαλασσία, = στρόμβος 2, Archil. 192; cf. σάλπη.

IV name of a bird, Hsch. (perh. = σαλπιγκτής 2).

V a kind of comet, Ptol. Tetr. 90.

VI epith. of Athena at Argos, Lyc. 915,986, Paus. 2.21.3.

n93166.head: σαλπίζω
n93166.html:
σαλπίζω, fut. -ιῶ LXX Nu. 10.4: aor. ἐσάλπιγξα X. An. 1.2.17, Archipp. 19; Ep. σάλπιγξα (v. infr.):—later, fut. σαλπίσω 1 Ep.Cor. 15.52: aor. ἐσάλπισα LXX Jo. 6.13, Luc. Ocyp. 114, Ath. 4.130b, etc.:—Pass., pf. σεσάλπιγκται (περι-) Eudamidas ap. Stob. 4.13.65:—σαλπίσσω is Tarentine, Eust. 1654.24, An.Ox. 1.62; σαλπίττω Att., ap. Phot., Luc. Jud.Voc. 10, v.l. in Poll. 4.86; σαλπίδδω Boeot., An.Ox. 4.325:—

sound the trumpet, σάλπιγξι ῥυθμοὺς σ. X. An. 7.3.32: c. acc. cogn., σ. πολέμου κτύπον Batr. 200; σ. ἀνακλητικόν AP 11.136 (Lucill.); λιγὺν ἦχον Hedyl. ap. Ath. 11.497d; τὸ . . δείπνου σημεῖον Ath. 4.130b: abs., ὅταν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου Ev.Matt. 6.2: metaph., ἀμφὶ δὲ σάλπιγξεν μέγας οὐρανός heaven trumpeted around, Il. 21.388: impers., ἐπεὶ ἐσάλπιγξε (sc. ὁ σαλπιγκτής) when the trumpet sounded, X. An. 1.2.17, cf. 1 Ep.Cor. 15.52.

2 c. acc., ἡμέραν σ. proclaim, announce day, of the cock, Luc. Ocyp. 114.

n93168.head: σάλπισμα
n93168.html:
σάλπισμα, ατος, τό,

trumpet-call, Poll. 4.86; σαλπισμός, ὁ, Thd. Nu. 23.21.

n93171.head: σαλπιστικός
n93171.html:
σαλπιστικός, ή, όν,

of or for a trumpet, κρούματα Poll. 4.84.

n93174.head: σαλτάριος
n93174.html:
σαλτάριος, ὁ,

= Lat. salt(u)arius, IGRom. 4.634 (Phrygia), 1186 (Lydia), prob. in Rev.Arch. 1904 i 20 (Thrace, iii A.D.).

n93175.head: σαλύγη
n93175.html:
σαλύγη, ἡ,

constant motion, as of the spindle, Hsch.

n93176.head: σάλυξ
n93176.html: σάλυξ, ἡ, f.l. for κάλυξ, Ps.-Dsc. 4.23.

n93178.head: σαλώμη
n93178.html:
σαλώμη, ἡ,

a medicine (prob. from the pr. n.), Androm. ap. Gal. 13.507.

n93180.head: σαλώτια
n93180.html:
σαλώτια, pl.,

dub. sens. (in list of eatables, etc.), POxy. 920.5 (ii/ iii A.D.); ῥίζια δύο σαλωτίων Sammelb. 1.25 (iii A.D.); cf. σαλούσιον.

n93182.head: σαμαγόρειος
n93182.html: σαμαγόρειος οἶνος, ὁ, a kind of wine, Arist. Fr. 109.

n93184.head: Σάμαινα
n93184.html:
Σάμαινα [Σᾰ], ἡ, (Σάμος)

a ship of Samian build, Plu. Per. 26; used as a stamp on Samian coins, Duris 66 J., cf. Hsch. s.v. Σαμιακὸς τρόπος (= Cratin. 13), Head Hist.Num. 2p.603.

n93186.head: σαμάκιον
n93186.html: σαμάκιον, τό, an article of female attire, Com.Adesp. 1136.

n93187.head: σάμαξ
n93187.html:
σάμαξ [σᾰ], ᾰκος, ὁ,

rush-mat, used as a bed in war, Chionid. 1; also, = τοξικὸς κάλαμος, Lysipp. 10.

n93188.head: Σαμάρεια
n93188.html:
Σαμάρεια [ᾰρ], ἡ,

Samaria, a city of Palestine, called Sebaste by Herod, Str. 16.2.34, etc.; also as name of a region, Ev.Luc. 17.11, etc.; of a village in Egypt, PEnteux. 8.6, al. (iii B.C.), PPetr. 2 p.14, al. (iii B.C.):—Σᾰμᾰρίτης [ῑ], ου (Dor. Σαμαρ-ίτας IG 12(8).439 (Thasos, ii B.C.)), ὁ, Samaritan, Ev.Matt. 10.5, etc.; fem. Σαμαρ-ῖτις, ιδος, Ev.Jo. 4.9, IG 3.2892 (Σαμαρ-εῖτις ib. 2891):—also Σᾰμᾰρεύς, έως, St.Byz., Suid.

n93192.head: σαμβαλούχη
n93192.html:
σαμβαλούχη, ἡ,

shoe-case, Herod. 7.19; also σαμβαλουχίς, ίδος, ἡ, ib. 53.

n93193.head: σαμβύκη
n93193.html:
σαμβύκη [ῡ], ἡ,

a triangular musical instrument with four strings, Arist. Pol. 1341b1, Neanth. 5 J., Juba 73; of barbaric origin, Str. 10.3.17. (Aramaic sabbekhā (perh. not Semitic), with m inserted, as in Ἀμβακούμ = Habakkuk. etc.).

2 = σαμβυκίστρια, Plb. 5.37.10; with pun on signf. II, Id. 8.6.6.

II an engine of like form used in sieges, Id. 8.4.8, al., Bito 57.1, Plu. Marc. 15, Ath.Mech. 27.7, App. Mith. 26.—Cf. σάμβυξ. [Penult. long in sambūca, Pers. 5.95.]

n93194.head: σαμβυκιστής
n93194.html:
σαμβυκιστής, οῦ, ὁ,

player on the σαμβύκη, Euph. ap. Ath. 4.182e:— fem. σαμβυκ-ίστρια, Philem. 44.5, Plu. Cleom. 35, Ant. 9.

n93195.head: σάμβυξ
n93195.html:
σάμβυξ, ὁ,

= σαμβύκη, Plb. 5.37.10, as cited by Suid.

n93196.head: σάμεα
n93196.html:
σάμεα, ων, τά,

marks on the edge of the dress (Lacon.), Hsch.

n93197.head: σαμεῖον
n93197.html: σαμεῖον, τό, Dor. for σημεῖον, Archyt. 1.

n93198.head: σαμένορα
n93198.html: σαμένορα τὸν βραβευτὴν τῶν σφαιριζόντων, Hsch.

n93199.head: σάμερον
n93199.html:
σάμερον,

v. σήμερον. Σάμη, v. Σάμος. σαμία, v. ζημία. σαμίθη· ῥόφημά τι, ὡς Γλαυκίας ὁ ἰατρός, Hsch. σαμινά, Lacon. for θαμινά, Id. σάμμα· ὄργανον μουσικὸν παρὰ Ἰνδοῖς, Id.

n93200.head: Σαμοθρᾴκη
n93200.html:
Σαμοθρᾴκη, Ion. Σαμοθρηΐκη, ἡ,

Samothrace, Hdt. 6.47; the seat of the mysteries of the Cabeiri, Id. 2.51; called Σάμος Θρηϊκίη in Hom., Il. 13.12, h.Ap. 34; and simply Σάμος, Il. 24.78, 753. Adj. Σᾰμόθρᾳξ (not Σαμοθρᾴξ), Hdn.Gr. 1.42, Choerob. in Theod. 1.187 H., etc.; Ion. pl. Σαμοθρήϊκες Hdt. 2.51, 8.90; also Σᾰμοθρᾴκιος, Ion. Σαμοθρηΐκιος, η, ον, Id. 7.59, 108.

n93201.head: Σαμοθρᾳκιασταί
n93201.html:
Σαμοθρᾳκιασταί, οἱ,

celebrators of Samothracian mysteries, IG 12(1).43, al., Michel 1307 (Teos), Supp.Epigr. 4.168 (Caria).

n93202.head: Σαμοθρᾴκιον
n93202.html:
Σαμοθρᾴκιον, τό,

temple of the gods of Samothrace, Jahresh. 26 Beibl. 54 (Ephesus, i A.D., in form -κιν).

n93203.head: Σάμος
n93203.html:
Σάμος [ᾰ], ἡ,

Samos, the name of several Greek islands:

1 old name for Κεφαλληνία (q.v.), Il. 2.634, Od. 4.671; also called Σάμη, 1.246, h.Ap. 429; though this, acc. to others, is a town on the island: hence Adj. Σαμαῖος, α, ον, Str. 10.2.13.

2 Σάμος Θρηϊκίη, v. Σαμοθρᾴκη.

3 Samos, the large island over against Ephesus, first in h.Ap. 41: hence Adj. Σάμιος, α, ον, Hdt. 1.70, etc.; ἡ Σαμία (sc. γῆ) ibid., Thphr. Lap. 62; also Σ. ἀστήρ, clay with medicinal properties, Gal. 12.178:—Σαμιακός, ή, όν, Cratin. 13. (Acc. to Str. 8.3.19, 10.2.17, σάμος was an old word signifying a height.)

n93204.head: σαμοῦχος
n93204.html: σαμοῦχος λίθος, name of a kind of stone, PMag.Par. 2.200.

n93206.head: σαμυλίς
n93206.html: σαμυλίς ἡ πρόπολις ὑπὸ τῶν μελισσουργῶν, Hsch.

n93207.head: σαμφαριτική
n93207.html:
σαμφαριτική νάρδος, ἡ,

camel-hay, Cymbopogon Schoenanthus, Dsc. 1.7.

n93208.head: σαμφόρας
n93208.html:
σαμφόρας, ου, ὁ, (φέρω)

horse branded with the letter σάν (v. Σ ς B. 2), Ar. Eq. 603, Nu. 122, 1298, Eust. 785.30.
n93208.gloss: a horse branded with the archaic letter san

n93209.head: σαμψήρα
n93209.html:
σαμψήρα, ἡ,

a kind of sword of state, J. AJ 20.2.3, cf. Suid.; written σαμσειρα, PGiss. 47.11 (ii A.D.). (Persian šamšīr.)

n93210.head: σαμψουχίζω
n93210.html:
σαμψουχίζω,

resemble marjoram, τῇ ὀσμῇ Dsc. 3.38.

2 flavour or scent with marjoram, in Pass., Id. 2.76.14.

n93211.head: σαμψούχινος
n93211.html:
σαμψούχινος, η, ον,

of marjoram, Dsc. 1.48, Gal. 6.291, Aët. 4.42. (Written -ψιχ- in Aët. l.c., cf. sq. [σάμψουχον])

n93212.head: σάμψουχον
n93212.html:
σάμψουχον, τό, foreign name of ἀμάρακος or

marjoram, Origanum majorana, Nic. Th. 617, Dsc. 3.39, Paus. 9.28.3, IG 14.2508 (Nemausus); written -ψυχ- in Aret. CA 2.6, cf. 10; gender indeterm. in Poll. 6.107.

n92017.head: σάν
n92017.html:
σάν (Greek name prob. σάν (v. Σ ς B. 2),

eighteenth letter in the Etruscan abecedaria (IG 14.2420) and probably in the oldest Gr. alphabets, occupying the same serial position as the Hebrew Tsade (צ, Phoenician 𐤑 Syria 6.103), with which it may be identified. In many of the oldest Gr. alphabets it represents the sound s, for which 𐌔 and Σ (twenty-first letter in the Etruscan abecedaria) is an alternative representation preferred in other Gr. alphabets. It is uncertain whether the letter Ͳ (name and serial position unknown), which represents the sound σσ in Schwyzer 707 (Ephesus, vi B.C.), 701A 17 (Erythrae, v B.C.), SIG 4.6 (Cyzicus, vi B.C.), 45.2, al. (Halic., v B.C.) and the third sound (σσ?) in the name of Mesambria in BMus.Cat.Coins Thrace p.132, is to be identified with Ϻ.

It is also uncertain whether the numerical symbol Ϡ (= 900), described by Gal. 17(1).525, which has this form in PEleph. 1 (iv B.C.), PCair.Zen. 22.5 (iii B.C.), Rev.Phil. 35.138 (Thessaly, iii B.C.), Milet. 6.39 (ii B.C.), where it forms part of a symbol for thousands, and later the forms Ͳ JHS 26.287 (Athenian tesserae of iv B.C.), 25.342 (papyri of ii B.C.), SIG 695.83 (Magn. Mae., ii B.C.), IG 12(1).913 (Rhodes, i B.C.), [see print copy] ib. 2(2).2776.11, al. (ii A.D.), and ϡ (medieval Mss., called παρακύϊσμα in Sch. D.T. p.496 H.), is to be identified with either of the foregoing. The numerical symbol, in the form [see print copy], follows ω in an Attic abecedarium, Bullettino dell’ Inst. di corrisp. archeol. 1867.75, and that position tallies with its numerical value, since ω = 800. The extended alphabet used by Archim. Spir. 11, Aequil. 2.3 for a diagram ends with Ω Ϡ Ϙ.
n92017.gloss: san, eighteenth letter in Etruscan alphabets

corr.why: Current drops the opening parenthesis (leaving 'Syria 6.103)' unbalanced) and the Hebrew צ, and puts the word Sadi where the Phoenician glyph stands. B keeps '(צ, Phoenician 𐤑' but adds its own note '[glyph variant of Phoenecian Sadi]', which is not LSJ text. The replacement begins with a space and yields: Tsade (צ, Phoenician 𐤑 Syria 6.103).
corr.quote: Hebrew Tsade (צ, Phoenician [glyph variant of Phoenecian Sadi] 𐤑 Syria 6.103)

corr.why: The glyph is an alternative way of writing the sound s alongside Σ (the Etruscan twenty-first letter), so it must be a sigma form. Current's ϟ is the koppa character, the subject of the next article, and cannot stand for s. B's 𐌔 encodes the three-stroke sigma.

Current has lost the glyph ('the numerical symbol  (= 900) ... which has this form'), and the sentence needs a symbol. The sign for 900 is sampi, and B supplies Ϡ, keeping it distinct from the later forms it marks separately.

Current's Τ is Greek tau (value 300), the wrong letter for the T-shaped later form of the 900 sign on Athenian tesserae. B uses the same archaic-sampi character here and for the Ionic σσ letter, so the printed glyph is the same in both places. Current writes that glyph as capital Ͳ, so Ͳ keeps the article consistent; B's lowercase ͳ would not.
corr.quote: It is uncertain whether the letter Ͳ (name and serial position unknown)

corr.why: Current has only a [see print copy] placeholder for the medieval-manuscript form of the 900 sign. B supplies the minuscule sampi ϡ, which is that form, while still marking unencodable variants elsewhere with notes. So ϡ reflects the printed glyph and fills the gap.
corr.quote: and ϡ (medieval Mss., called παρακύϊσμα in Sch.D.T.p.496 H.)

n93213b.head: σάναπτιν
n93213b.html: σάναπτιν τὴν οἰνώτην, Σκύσαι, Hsch.

n93213c.head: σανδαία
n93213c.html: σανδαία τροπὴ ἀπὸ γῆς, ἔνιοι δὲ τὸν λίβα ἄνεμον, Hsch.

n93214.head: σανδάλιον
n93214.html:
σανδάλιον [ᾰ], τό, Dim. of σάνδαλον, mostly in pl.,

sandals, Hdt. 2.91 (sg.), Cratin. 131, Cephisod. 4, LXX Jo. 9.5.

2 horseshoe, σ. ὀνικά POxy. 741.10 (ii A.D.).

II a surgical bandage, Heliod. (?)ap. Orib. 49.35.3, as v.l. for σανδάλιος, ὁ, which is found also in Heraclas ap. eund. 48.4.

III v. σάνδαλον II.

n93215.head: σανδαλίς
n93215.html:
σανδαλίς, ίδος, ἡ,

a kind of date, Plin. HN 13.43.

n93216.head: σανδαλίσκος
n93216.html: σανδαλίσκος, ὁ, Dim. of σάνδαλον, Ar. Ra. 406 (s.v.l., τὸ -κον Blass):—also σαμβᾰλίσκος, ὁ, heterocl. pl. -ίσκα, Hippon. 18.

n93218.head: σάνδαλον
n93218.html:
σάνδαλον, τό,

sandal, Eup. 295; mostly in pl., sandals, h.Merc. 79,83,139, etc.; Aeol. σάμβᾰλον Eumel. 13 K., Sapph. 98, AP 6.267 (Diotim.).

II a flat fish, Matro Conv. 76; also σανδάλιον, identified by Hsch. with ψῆττα, but distinguished from it by Alciphr. 1.7.

n93219.head: σανδαλώδης
n93219.html:
σανδαλώδης, ες,

sandal-like, Sch. E. Or. 1370.

n93220.head: σάνδανον
n93220.html:
σάνδανον, τό,

perh. sandal-wood, Santalum album, in pl., Aët. 16.142 (dub. sens., cf. σαγάλινος).

n93221.head: σανδαράκη
n93221.html:
σανδαράκη [ρᾰ], ἡ,

red sulphide of arsenic, realgar, Arist. HA 604b28, Plin. HN 34.177, Peripl.M.Rubr. 49; written σανδαράχη in Hp. Morb. 2.14 (but σανδαράκη Superf. 32), Dsc. 5.105, Gal. 17(1).834, Alciphr. 1.33, etc.

2 an orange pigment made therefrom, Thphr. Lap. 40, 50. (Assyr. šindu arḳu ‘green paint’, i.e. yellow sulphide of arsenic, orpiment, cf. ἀρσενικόν.)

II bee-bread, Arist. HA 626a7.

n93222.head: σανδαρακίζω
n93222.html:
σανδαρακίζω, v.l. σανδᾰρα-χίζω,

to be bright red, Dsc. 5.104.

n93223.head: σανδαράκινος
n93223.html:
σανδαράκινος, η, ον,

of orange colour, Hdt. 1.98, Ael. NA 17.23, Philostr. VA 3.14:—also σανδᾰρᾰχώδης, ες, Ruf. Fr. 67.4, Gal. 17(1).834.
